chunks: Uthman bin Abu Shayba said: Jareer narrated to me, from Hussayn bin Abdurrahman, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'After me, twelve emirs will arise.' He said: Then he spoke something that I did not hear, so I asked the people and asked my father, who was closer to him than I was, and he said: He said: 'All of them are from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and origin of the leaders after him?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, establishes the foundational Sunni-Shia consensus on the number of twelve caliphs, with the specific qualification that they must be from Quraysh. While Sunnis generally interpret this as a historical succession of twelve specific rulers, Shia scholarship emphasizes the divine appointment (*nass*) of these twelve Imams, viewing this narration as a key proof for the Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt.
